q: How should the six named species of the Enterobacter cloacae complex (E. cloacae, E. hormaechei, E. asburiae, E. kobei, E. ludwigii, E. nimipressuralis) be reconciled when ANI/whole-genome-based species boundaries disagree with the older biochemical + MLST-based classifications that placed all of the Liu et al. (2013) 'E. cloacae' strains (ENHKU01, ATCC13047, EcWSU1, SDM) under a single species label?
basis: Liu 2013 treats ENHKU01, ATCC13047, EcWSU1 and SDM as four E. cloacae strains and builds a 4-strain core/pan-genome (3540 shared CDS per paper, 3345 in this replication; 4a/4b in REPORT.md). But this replication measured whole-proteome AAI within that 4-strain group at only 93.6-94.0%, which is exactly at/near the ANI/AAI species-boundary threshold (~94-95% AAI); i.e. some of these 'E. cloacae' strains may actually belong to sister complex members (e.g. hormaechei/kobei) under a modern genome-based taxonomy. The paper predates the current wave of complex-wide ANI reclassifications.
next_steps: Compute pairwise ANI (pyani ANIm/ANIb or skani) on the same 4 assemblies plus modern complex-type strains (E. hormaechei ATCC 49162, E. asburiae ATCC 35953, E. kobei DSM 13645, E. ludwigii EN-119, E. nimipressuralis DSM 30177) and place each Liu 2013 'E. cloacae' strain against the 95%-ANI species cutoff.

Rebuild the Liu 2013 core/pan-genome analysis at the true species boundary (whichever subset of the 4 strains actually falls above 95% ANI to E. cloacae s.s. ATCC 13047) and check whether the pan-genome plasticity ordering still holds.
Compare AAI, ANI, dDDH (GGDC) and rMLST-based species calls on the same 4 strains to quantify which methods agree at the complex boundary.

q: Is the pan-genome divergence between clinical E. cloacae isolates (e.g. ATCC13047, human bloodstream) and environmental/plant-associated E. cloacae isolates (e.g. ENHKU01 pepper endophyte, EcWSU1 plant pathogen, SDM 2,3-butanediol producer) large enough and structured enough to define a stable hospital-adaptation gene signature, or is the difference dominated by generic strain-plasticity variance?
basis: This replication reproduced Liu 2013's strain-unique-CDS ordering almost exactly (ATCC13047 19.8% unique vs paper 20%; EcWSU1 13.3% vs 12%; ENHKU01 7.8% vs ~6%; SDM 7.1% vs ~6% -- section 4b of REPORT.md). ATCC13047 -- the only clinical isolate in the set -- is a dramatic outlier in accessory-genome size and carries 2 plasmids while the others have 0 or 1. But n=1 clinical isolate cannot separate 'hospital-adaptation signal' from 'individual-strain plasticity noise'.
next_steps: Assemble a matched cohort of at least 20 clinical E. cloacae vs 20 environmental E. cloacae genomes from NCBI/BV-BRC and rerun the Liu 2013 DIAMOND-RBH pan/core pipeline at the same 50%id/70%cov thresholds.

Test whether accessory-genome enrichment for AMR / heavy-metal-resistance / biofilm / plasmid-replicon gene families is significantly higher in the clinical subset (Scoary or Roary + gene-wise Fisher).

Ask whether the ATCC13047 20%-unique-CDS signal collapses to the population mean once >=20 clinical isolates are included, which would recast it as strain-level plasticity rather than a clinical-adaptation signature.

q: How diverse are the mobile genetic elements (plasmids, integrative conjugative elements, IS elements, prophages) that carry blaAmpC and carbapenemase / ESBL genes across the E. cloacae complex, and does the plasmid catalogue of ATCC13047 (2 plasmids, source of the '>20 variable regions' claim) generalise to clinical E. cloacae as a class?
basis: Liu 2013 -- and this replication -- confirm ATCC13047 carries 2 plasmids and >20 variable regions on its chromosome (C3 in REPORT.md), and the paper flags 'variable regions carrying strain-specific virulence' and AMR as one of three headline findings. But Liu 2013 did not systematically type plasmid Inc groups, did not resolve which MGEs carry which AMR genes, and only had 4 E. cloacae genomes to work with. The current AMR/ESBL/carbapenemase burden of the complex is a major clinical concern that the 2013 paper predates.
next_steps: Rerun on the 4 Liu 2013 genomes: PlasmidFinder / MOB-suite for plasmid replicon typing + AMRFinderPlus / ResFinder for blaAmpC / KPC / NDM / VIM / IMP / OXA-48 detection, and localise each AMR gene to chromosome vs plasmid vs ICE vs prophage.

Extend to a modern set of >=100 complete E. cloacae complex genomes and cluster plasmids by ANI + backbone content to test whether a small number of dominant AMR-plasmid backbones account for most carbapenemase carriage.
Cross-reference MGE-carried AMR genes against the '>20 variable regions' coordinates on ATCC13047 to test whether those regions are the same integrative hotspots seen in modern isolates.

q: Does the differential presence of T3SS, T6SS, and fimbriae repertoires across the E. cloacae complex define a reproducible pathogenicity gradient, or are these gene-repertoire differences uncorrelated with clinical / colonisation outcome?
basis: This replication cleanly reproduced the T6SS rank-ordering on 2 of 4 strains (ATCC13047 = 2, SDM = 1) but under-called on ENHKU01 (1 clear + 1 fragmented vs paper's 2) and EcWSU1 (0 vs 1) because the paper's T6SS calls used manual curation + BLAST reconfirmation (section 4d of REPORT.md). Fimbrial-locus counts landed in the paper's 8-19 range but 'only 4 conserved across all 4' was not cleanly re-demonstrated. Liu 2013 asserts these repertoires underlie host/niche determination but does not test the gradient beyond 4 strains.
next_steps: Run a dedicated secretion-system caller (SecReT6, TXSScan/MacSyFinder T3SS_1/T3SS_2, T4SEfinder) on a curated panel of >=50 E. cloacae complex genomes stratified by isolation source (bloodstream / respiratory / urinary / plant endophyte / soil).
Score fimbrial CU-pathway repertoires (FimTyper or CUPP-family HMMs) on the same panel and test for significant enrichment differences by isolation source.

Correlate T6SS/T3SS/fimbriae counts with clinical severity metadata (BSI vs colonisation, mortality) where available, and against in-vitro competition/adherence assays to test whether the gene-repertoire gradient predicts phenotype.

q: How congruent is the whole-genome / core-genome phylogenetic topology of the Enterobacter genus with the topologies produced by rMLST, single-locus 16S rRNA (rrs), and single-locus dnaJ trees that dominated pre-2013 Enterobacter taxonomy, and where do the incongruences fall?
basis: This replication reproduced Liu 2013's genus-level topology via an independent AAI/NJ tree (E. cloacae strains form a tight clade at 93.6-94.0% AAI, Pantoea outgroup separates cleanly at 72-73% AAI, E. aerogenes falls basally consistent with its known reclassification as Klebsiella aerogenes -- section 4c of REPORT.md). But the paper's tree is a 1732-core-gene MrBayes tree and my AAI/NJ is method-agnostic; the paper did not test explicitly against rMLST / 16S / dnaJ topologies, and the whole-proteome AAI signal was too coarse to resolve C7 ('ENHKU01 closest to ATCC13047', which was originally a 4-housekeeping-gene call).
next_steps: Extract rMLST (53 ribosomal-protein loci), full-length 16S rRNA (rrs), and dnaJ sequences from the 8 Enterobacter + 3 Pantoea genomes used by Liu 2013 and build one tree per marker with the same substitution model.

Compare each single-locus / rMLST tree against the whole-genome AAI-NJ and the paper's 1732-core-gene MrBayes tree using RF / matching-split / Kendall-Colijn distances and identify which branches disagree.

Specifically test whether the C7 'ENHKU01 closest to ATCC13047' result is a locus-sampling artifact of the 4 housekeeping genes used by Liu 2013 by resampling small marker sets and measuring nearest-neighbor volatility.
